URL path settings
Uncheck this to create a custom alias below. Configure URL alias patterns.
Optionally specify an alternative URL by which this content can be accessed. For example, type "about" when writing an about page. Use a relative path and don't add a trailing slash or the URL alias won't work.
XML sitemap
The priority of this URL relative to other URLs on your site.
Meta tags

Configure the meta tags below. Tokens, e.g. "[node:summary]", automatically insert the corresponding information from that field or value, which helps to avoid redundant meta data and possible search engine penalization; see the "Browse available tokens" popup for more details.

Hide Basic tags
The text to display in the title bar of a visitor's web browser when they view this page. This meta tag may also be used as the title of the page when a visitor bookmarks or favorites this page, or as the page title in a search engine result. It is common to append '[site:name]' to the end of this, so the site's name is automatically added. It is recommended that the title be no greater than 55 - 65 characters long, including spaces.
Content limited to 380 characters, remaining: 366
A brief and concise summary of the page's content that is a maximum of 160 characters in length. The description meta tag may be used by search engines to display a snippet about the page in search results. This will be truncated to a maximum of 380 characters after any tokens are processsed.
A comma-separated list of keywords about the page. This meta tag is no longer supported by most search engines anymore.
Show Advanced tags
Provides search engines with specific directions for what to do when this page is indexed.
The URl of the preferred page location or URL of the content of this page, to help eliminate duplicate content penalties from search engines.
Show Open Graph
The Open Graph meta tags(link is external and opens in a new window) are used control how Facebook, Pinterest, LinkedIn and other social networking sites interpret the content of the site.

The Facebook Sharing Debugger(link is external and opens in a new window) lets you preview how your content will look when shared to Facebook and debug any issues with your Open Graph tags.
The title of the content, e.g., The Rock.
Show Twitter card
A set of meta tags specially for controlling the summaries displayed when content is shared on Twitter(link is external and opens in a new window).
Content limited to 70 characters, remaining: 70
The page's title, which should be concise; it will be truncated at 70 characters by Twitter. This field is required unless this the 'type' field is set to "photo". This will be truncated to a maximum of 70 characters after any tokens are processsed.
Revision information
Provide an explanation of the changes you are making. This will help other authors understand your motivations.
Shield settings

Temporarily hide this content behind a basic authentication shield. Do not use to hide sensitive information, use only for low-risk content staging, this is not a permanent or reliable privacy solution.
